claims.text: A hybrid atomistic simulation using a new many-body potential will predict the thermal conductivity of oxygen-containing bulk HfNbTaTiZr more accurately than existing perfect-crystal analytical models.
The relevant initial material is an as-cast bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimen containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The proposed many-body potential can explicitly account for oxygen-defect scattering in the multi-principal-element lattice.
Experimental thermal-conductivity data already partially exist for oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr in the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K intervals.
Approximately 1 wt.% oxygen acts as point defects in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen point defects influence phonon scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen point defects influence electron scattering in HfNbTaTiZr.
HfNbTaTiZr may exhibit BCC, HCP, or disordered phases under the stated conditions.
Existing analytical conductivity models for HfNbTaTiZr assume perfect crystal lattices and omit realistic impurity scattering.
Including realistic defect-scattering channels will correct the perfect-lattice oversimplification and reduce conductivity-prediction errors.
The new framework will reduce disagreement with measured conductivity by several percent across both 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Analytical models calibrated for nominally pure, defect-free HfNbTaTiZr show relatively large conductivity discrepancies, especially above 300 K and in the cryogenic regime.
Defect scattering is significant for HfNbTaTiZr thermal conductivity in the cryogenic regime.
The proposed approach is applicable to bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing up to approximately 1–2 wt.% oxygen.
Prediction quality may degrade above approximately 2 wt.% oxygen.
Prediction quality may degrade if large secondary phases form.
The expected error reduction is approximately 5–15%.
The exact quantitative improvement cannot be established without larger datasets.
